sources.locus: SS68 - Antony's own rejection of Melitian communion and, when Arians came to him, his response driving them away

quotes.speaker_or_author: Athanasius, narrating Antony's own action - not Antony's own reported speech
quotes.text: He drove them from the mountain, saying that their words were worse than the poison of serpents.

sources.locus: SS19 - from Antony's extended discourse to the gathered brothers

quotes.text: ...let us hold fast our discipline, and let us not be careless... But to avoid being heedless, it is good to consider the word of the Apostle, 'I die daily.' For if we too live as though dying daily, we shall not sin... For our life is naturally uncertain, and Providence allots it to us daily.

sources.locus: SS69 - Antony, summoned to Alexandria by the bishops, publicly teaching against the Arians

quotes.text: ...the Son of God was not a created being, neither had He come into being from non-existence, but that He was the Eternal Word and Wisdom of the Essence of the Father. And therefore it was impious to say, 'there was a time when He was not,' for the Word was always co-existent with the Father.

sources.locus: SS9 - Antony's own words to the demons attacking him in beast form

quotes.text: If there had been any power in you, it would have sufficed had one of you come, but since the Lord hath made you weak, you attempt to terrify me by numbers: and a proof of your weakness is that you take the shapes of brute beasts... If you are able, and have received power against me, delay not to attack; but if you are unable, why trouble me in vain? For faith in our Lord is a seal and a wall of safety to us.

sources.locus: Arsenius, Alphabetical Collection - a widely attested saying attributed to Arsenius, given here in plain English rather than a specific published translation's own wording

quotes.speaker_or_author: a voice Arsenius reports having heard
quotes.text: Flee the company of men, and you will be saved... Flee, be silent, be still - these are the roots of a life without sin.

sources.locus: Moses, Alphabetical Collection - a widely attested saying of Abba Moses's, given here in plain English rather than a specific published translation's own wording

quotes.text: My own sins run out behind me the same way, and I do not see them - and today I am coming to judge another man's fault.

sources.locus: ch. XXXII - the angel's own opening instruction, in Clarke's translation

quotes.text: Thou shalt allow each man to eat and drink according to his strength; and proportionately to the strength of the eaters appoint to them their labours. And prevent no man either from fasting or eating.

sources.locus: Sarah, Alphabetical Collection - a widely attested saying of Amma Sarah's, given here in plain English rather than a specific published translation's own wording

quotes.text: By nature I am a woman, but not by my own thoughts. It is I who am the man here, and you who are the women.
